launch-tx-austin-zilker-metropolitan-par.summary: Austin's landmark metropolitan park combines the Great Lawn, Barton Springs Pool, family play, gardens, nature exhibits, trails, river access, sports, performances, and major events in one large campus.
launch-tx-austin-zilker-metropolitan-par.hours: General park hours are 5:00 a.m.-10:00 p.m.; Barton Springs Pool and individual attractions keep separate schedules.
launch-tx-austin-zilker-metropolitan-par.parking: Parking is spread across several lots. Weekends, holidays, festivals, and swim days fill quickly; seasonal paid parking and event traffic plans may apply. Match the lot to your destination rather than entering 'Zilker Park' alone.
launch-tx-austin-zilker-metropolitan-par.arrival: Use Barton Springs Road for the playscape, Great Lawn, pool, and theater; use Stratford Drive or destination-specific entrances for the nature center, garden, disc golf, and lake side.
launch-tx-austin-zilker-metropolitan-par.restrooms: Restrooms are available near major facilities, but hours and closures vary. Barton Springs Pool, the garden, nature center, and theater have their own facilities and admission boundaries.
launch-tx-austin-zilker-metropolitan-par.cost: The general park is free. Barton Springs Pool, Zilker Botanical Garden, train rides, rentals, reservations, parking periods, and ticketed events can charge fees.
launch-tx-austin-zilker-metropolitan-par.accessibility: Accessible parking and routes serve major destinations, but the campus is large and includes slopes, gravel, grass, creek banks, and event detours. Choose the exact feature before navigating.
launch-tx-austin-zilker-metropolitan-par.dogs: Leashed dogs may use ordinary park areas; pets are restricted from Barton Springs Pool, some attractions, play areas, and event zones. Observe posted rules.
launch-tx-austin-zilker-metropolitan-par.family: The playscape, miniature train, nature center, gardens, Great Lawn, and guarded pool hours are major family draws. Heat, water safety, crowds, and long walks between attractions need planning.
launch-tx-austin-zilker-metropolitan-par.transit: CapMetro Route 30 serves Barton Springs Road. Walking and biking connections reach the park from the Butler Trail; special-event shuttles and road controls vary by event.
launch-tx-austin-zilker-metropolitan-par.need: Confirm pool and attraction hours separately, check live park closures, and expect major access changes for ACL Festival, Trail of Lights, holidays, flooding, maintenance, and large events. Barton Creek can rise quickly after rain.

launch-tx-austin-mueller-lake-park.summary: A 30-acre neighborhood destination built around a lake, paved loop, playground, lawns, picnic areas, Browning Hangar, public events, and connections through Mueller's trail network.
launch-tx-austin-mueller-lake-park.hours: Open during posted public park hours; events, the farmers market, and managed facilities use separate schedules.
launch-tx-austin-mueller-lake-park.parking: Use marked street spaces and public parking near Mueller Boulevard, Simond Avenue, Aldrich Street, or Browning Hangar. Event and market days increase demand; do not use reserved residential or business spaces.
launch-tx-austin-mueller-lake-park.arrival: Use 4550 Mueller Boulevard for the lake and central park; use the Browning Hangar or Aldrich Street destination when attending a scheduled event.
launch-tx-austin-mueller-lake-park.restrooms: Public restrooms are available near the playground and central park amenities, with additional facilities tied to events and nearby businesses.
launch-tx-austin-mueller-lake-park.cost: General park access is free. Markets, programs, food, rentals, and private events may charge separately.
launch-tx-austin-mueller-lake-park.accessibility: The paved lake loop, curb ramps, playground approaches, seating, and central amenities support accessible visits. Grass and crowded event areas can be less predictable.
launch-tx-austin-mueller-lake-park.dogs: Dogs are welcome on leash in ordinary park areas. Keep them away from playground equipment, maintain control near wildlife and crowds, and remove waste.
launch-tx-austin-mueller-lake-park.family: The playground, short lake loop, lawns, ducks, shaded seating, and nearby food make this a manageable family stop. Supervise children closely at the unfenced water edge.
launch-tx-austin-mueller-lake-park.transit: CapMetro routes serve Mueller, and protected bike/trail connections reach the park from surrounding neighborhoods. Check the trip planner for the nearest current stop.
launch-tx-austin-mueller-lake-park.need: The lake is visual habitat, not a swimming area. Shade is uneven, event days change parking and lawn access, and the nearby Bartholomew Splash Pad is a separate destination.

launch-tx-austin-mckinney-falls-state-pa.summary: An Austin state park centered on Upper and Lower Falls along Onion Creek, with swimming and fishing when conditions allow, nearly nine miles of trails, camping, cabins, historic sites, picnicking, and bouldering.
launch-tx-austin-mckinney-falls-state-pa.hours: Open daily; gate hours are 8:00 a.m.-10:00 p.m. and the office is generally 8:00 a.m.-4:15 p.m. Visitor Center hours are shorter.
launch-tx-austin-mckinney-falls-state-pa.parking: Enter through headquarters and follow the park map to Upper Falls, Lower Falls, trailheads, campsites, or cabins. The park often reaches capacity, so reserve a day pass before driving out.
launch-tx-austin-mckinney-falls-state-pa.arrival: Use the main entrance at 5808 McKinney Falls Parkway. Stop at headquarters for current creek conditions and destination-specific directions.
launch-tx-austin-mckinney-falls-state-pa.restrooms: Restrooms are available in developed day-use and camping areas. Primitive trail and creek locations may be far from facilities.
launch-tx-austin-mckinney-falls-state-pa.cost: $6 daily for adults age 13 and older; children 12 and under enter free. Camping, cabins, and other facilities cost extra. Current pass rules control.
launch-tx-austin-mckinney-falls-state-pa.accessibility: A 2.8-mile hard-surface route supports strollers and road bikes, and all-terrain wheelchairs may be available. Falls, creek banks, boulders, and natural trails are rugged.
launch-tx-austin-mckinney-falls-state-pa.dogs: Leashed pets are allowed in most outdoor areas but not inside buildings; keep pets out of swimming areas where posted and protect them from hot rock and creek hazards.
launch-tx-austin-mckinney-falls-state-pa.family: The falls, short trails, fishing, Junior Ranger activities, picnics, and camping suit families, but there are no lifeguards and slippery limestone, sudden depth, heat, and currents require close supervision.
launch-tx-austin-mckinney-falls-state-pa.transit: The park is not a convenient transit destination; most visitors drive or arrange a ride. Confirm return transportation because the entrance is separated from major attractions by park roads.
launch-tx-austin-mckinney-falls-state-pa.need: Reserve before visiting, review active alerts, and call for creek conditions after rain. Onion Creek can flood rapidly; swimming may be unsafe or unavailable even when the park itself is open.

launch-tx-austin-pease-district-park.summary: A Shoal Creek greenway park anchored by Kingsbury Commons, with imaginative play, a seasonal splash pad, Treehouse observation pod, nature play, basketball, lawns, Tudor Cottage, trails, and historic landscapes.
launch-tx-austin-pease-district-park.hours: Public areas follow posted park hours; Kingsbury Commons facilities, splash pad, reservations, and programs can use shorter or seasonal schedules.
launch-tx-austin-pease-district-park.parking: Parking is extremely limited. Walk, bike, use transit, or follow Pease Park's current parking guidance; do not assume a space will be available beside Kingsbury Commons.
launch-tx-austin-pease-district-park.arrival: Use 1100 Kingsbury Street for Kingsbury Commons. Trail users can enter from multiple Shoal Creek connections, but feature access and parking differ along the long park.
launch-tx-austin-pease-district-park.restrooms: Improved public restrooms are located at Kingsbury Commons. Northern trail sections have fewer facilities.
launch-tx-austin-pease-district-park.cost: General park entry, play areas, and the city splash pad are free. Reservations and ticketed programs may cost extra.
launch-tx-austin-pease-district-park.accessibility: Kingsbury Commons includes accessible routes and inclusive play elements. Shoal Creek trails, slopes, wet surfaces, and natural areas vary.
launch-tx-austin-pease-district-park.dogs: Leashed dogs may use ordinary park and trail areas. Keep pets out of designated play and splash-pad zones and under close control near children and creek habitat.
launch-tx-austin-pease-district-park.family: Kingsbury Commons concentrates the playground, Treehouse, nature play, splash pad, restrooms, picnic space, and open lawn into the easiest family visit.
launch-tx-austin-pease-district-park.transit: Walking, biking, and public transportation are strongly encouraged because parking is scarce. Check current CapMetro routing and Pease Park access guidance.
launch-tx-austin-pease-district-park.need: Check Austin's facility-closures page before a splash or nature-play visit. As of the latest city notice, portions of the western trail, splash pad, and nature play area are affected by a plumbing break and runoff until further notice.

launch-tx-austin-waterloo-park.summary: A downtown greenway park with Moody Amphitheater, Waller Creek trails, gardens, heritage trees, lawns, play space, public art, restrooms, and connections toward the Capitol and Lady Bird Lake.
launch-tx-austin-waterloo-park.hours: The park is generally open daily during posted hours; Moody Amphitheater events and production closures use separate schedules and entry rules.
launch-tx-austin-waterloo-park.parking: Use downtown garages, metered parking, transit, biking, or walking. The nearby Capitol Complex garage may offer limited public parking; event rates and street restrictions can change.
launch-tx-austin-waterloo-park.arrival: Use 500 East 12th Street for the park. Concert guests should follow the specific Moody Amphitheater ticket and gate instructions rather than ordinary park navigation.
launch-tx-austin-waterloo-park.restrooms: Public restrooms and water fountains are available in Waterloo Park; access can change during events or maintenance.
launch-tx-austin-waterloo-park.cost: Day-to-day park access is free. Ticketed concerts, premium areas, concessions, and special programs may cost extra.
launch-tx-austin-waterloo-park.accessibility: ADA-accessible paths connect gardens, lawns, play space, restrooms, and amphitheater areas. Event layouts may change routes and seating access.
launch-tx-austin-waterloo-park.dogs: Leashed dogs are allowed during ordinary park use; event policies may prohibit pets. Keep dogs out of planted beds and remove waste.
launch-tx-austin-waterloo-park.family: The playground, creek overlooks, lawns, gardens, and short downtown paths work well for families outside concert crowd periods.
launch-tx-austin-waterloo-park.transit: Downtown bus routes, nearby Red Line access, bikeways, and walking connections make transit preferable to event parking.
launch-tx-austin-waterloo-park.need: Check the park event calendar before visiting. Concert setup can close lawns or paths, and summer heat is strongest on exposed slopes despite substantial garden shade.

launch-tx-austin-butler-metro-park.summary: A downtown family park beside Palmer Events Center with the two-acre Alliance Children's Garden, Doug Sahm Hill skyline views, a pond, walking paths, lawns, and seasonal water play.
launch-tx-austin-butler-metro-park.hours: General park and Alliance Children's Garden hours are 5:00 a.m.-10:00 p.m. unless posted otherwise; splash-pad and event operations are seasonal or separate.
launch-tx-austin-butler-metro-park.parking: The Palmer Events Center garage is the most direct paid option. Nearby event schedules can affect rates, availability, and road access; trail and transit arrival may be easier.
launch-tx-austin-butler-metro-park.arrival: Use 1000 Barton Springs Road for Alliance Children's Garden. Doug Sahm Hill, the pond, and trail connections are spread across the park, so select the exact feature when navigating.
launch-tx-austin-butler-metro-park.restrooms: Public restrooms are available near the children's garden and event-center side, subject to posted hours and maintenance.
launch-tx-austin-butler-metro-park.cost: General park and children's garden access are free. Garage parking and ticketed Palmer Events Center activities cost separately; city splash pads do not charge admission when operating.
launch-tx-austin-butler-metro-park.accessibility: Alliance Children's Garden was designed for varied ages and abilities, with paved routes and multigenerational play. The observation hill has a significant grade.
launch-tx-austin-butler-metro-park.dogs: Pets are not permitted inside Alliance Children's Garden. Leashed dogs may use ordinary park paths and lawns where posted rules allow.
launch-tx-austin-butler-metro-park.family: Alliance Children's Garden is the main family draw, with themed play zones, climbing, slides, nature-inspired play, and nearby seasonal water play. Check surfaces for dangerous heat.
launch-tx-austin-butler-metro-park.transit: CapMetro routes serve Barton Springs Road and downtown; the Butler Trail and Pfluger Bridge provide strong walking and biking connections.
launch-tx-austin-butler-metro-park.need: The Liz Carpenter Splash Pad is seasonal and may close for repairs; verify the live city aquatics status before promising children water play. Palmer events can change parking and crowd levels.

launch-tx-austin-ann-and-roy-butler-hike.summary: Austin's highly visited 10-mile urban lake loop links downtown parks, boardwalks, bridges, skyline overlooks, cultural destinations, trailheads, boat access, and neighborhood connections.
launch-tx-austin-ann-and-roy-butler-hike.hours: The Boardwalk is open 5:00 a.m.-midnight daily, with a midnight-5:00 a.m. curfew. Connected parks and facilities may close earlier.
launch-tx-austin-ann-and-roy-butler-hike.parking: Choose a trailhead before driving. Festival Beach, International Shores, Auditorium Shores, street spaces, and other lots serve different loop segments; availability and payment rules vary.
launch-tx-austin-ann-and-roy-butler-hike.arrival: Do not navigate only to the trail name. Select the boardwalk, Festival Beach, Auditorium Shores, Pfluger Bridge, or another landmark closest to the segment you want.
launch-tx-austin-ann-and-roy-butler-hike.restrooms: Restrooms and water are available at selected parks and trailheads, including boardwalk-area facilities, but not continuously around the loop.
launch-tx-austin-ann-and-roy-butler-hike.cost: Trail and boardwalk access are free. Parking, rentals, events, food, and nearby attractions may charge.
launch-tx-austin-ann-and-roy-butler-hike.accessibility: The boardwalk and many urban sections are paved and accessible; much of the loop is decomposed granite, and grades, detours, flooding, crowding, and construction affect individual segments.
launch-tx-austin-ann-and-roy-butler-hike.dogs: Dogs are generally allowed on leash. Use only clearly designated off-leash areas, carry water, avoid hot surfaces, and keep pets out of Lady Bird Lake because of recurring harmful algae risk.
launch-tx-austin-ann-and-roy-butler-hike.family: Short out-and-back segments, boardwalk overlooks, bridges, turtles, skyline views, and connected playgrounds work better for young children than committing to the full 10-mile loop.
launch-tx-austin-ann-and-roy-butler-hike.transit: Downtown transit, bikeshare, neighborhood paths, and pedestrian bridges reach many trailheads. Select a start and finish before using a trip planner.
launch-tx-austin-ann-and-roy-butler-hike.need: I-35 reconstruction is causing long-term detours, intermittent closures, and water-access restrictions near the bridges through the construction period. Check live trail notices, heat, storms, algae advisories, and flood conditions.

launch-tx-austin-emma-long-metropolitan-.summary: A large Lake Austin destination with a designated swimming beach, boat ramps, day-use picnicking, reservable group sites, camping, open space, and the rugged Turkey Creek motorcycle and mountain-bike trail system.
launch-tx-austin-emma-long-metropolitan-.hours: Open year-round 7:00 a.m.-10:00 p.m.; the on-site office keeps shorter seasonal hours.
launch-tx-austin-emma-long-metropolitan-.parking: A paid entry pass is required. Peak-season Friday-Sunday and holiday visits require advance passes, often sell out, and do not allow roadside parking or entry without a valid pass.
launch-tx-austin-emma-long-metropolitan-.arrival: Use the City Park Road entrance and have the pass ready. Boat ramps, beach, picnic reservations, primitive campsites, and utility campsites have different internal routes.
launch-tx-austin-emma-long-metropolitan-.restrooms: Developed areas normally include toilets, showers, sinks, and water. Water utilities are planned to be shut off during August-October 2026 maintenance, leaving portable toilets while showers, sinks, fountains, and hose bibs are unavailable.
launch-tx-austin-emma-long-metropolitan-.cost: Current day-use fees are generally $5 per vehicle Monday-Thursday, $10 Friday-Sunday and holidays, and $1 for walk/bike entry; camping and reservations cost extra.
launch-tx-austin-emma-long-metropolitan-.accessibility: Developed picnic, beach, parking, and restroom areas provide accessible features, but shorelines, campsites, slopes, and Turkey Creek trails vary substantially.
launch-tx-austin-emma-long-metropolitan-.dogs: Leashed dogs may use allowed outdoor areas, but swimming-beach and facility restrictions may apply. Protect paws from heat and keep pets away from wildlife and unsafe water.
launch-tx-austin-emma-long-metropolitan-.family: The designated beach, picnic sites, shoreline, and camping support full-day family visits. There is no substitute for close water supervision, sun protection, and advance pass planning.
launch-tx-austin-emma-long-metropolitan-.transit: This is primarily a driving destination with limited practical transit access. Arrange transportation in advance and do not rely on roadside drop-off or parking outside the gate.
launch-tx-austin-emma-long-metropolitan-.need: Buy peak-season passes before travel, check boat-ramp and utility alerts, and confirm lake, storm, and water-quality conditions. Passes have no in/out privileges and capacity rules are enforced.
